title: Learned promoter models identify human-specific transcription motifs
summary: Models trained on promoter activity measurements helped characterize a human-specific downstream promoter variant and select synthetic motifs with species-specific activity. In-vitro transcription assays tested the predicted preferences with human and Drosophila extracts. These are gene-regulation and construct-assay findings, not demonstrated effects in organisms or disease.

evidence.tested: Predicted promoter preferences were compared with measured transcription in extracts.
evidence.unknown: Native-chromatin regulatory effects and organism-level outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: HARPE-trained support-vector regression supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Institutional manuscript abstract and selected SVR Methods; primary PubMed early-online date, affiliations and experimental figure captions.
